name: Dr. Maya Rowan
bio: Specializes in late 19th-century industrial laboratory accidents and the material culture of early thermodynamics. Former curator of scientific instruments.

name: Julian Vance
bio: Investigates lost institutional records, disputed patent wars, and the political entanglements of early modern optics and glassmaking.

name: Evelyn Moreau
bio: Explores how forgotten microscopists, midwives, and sanatorium chemists shaped our understanding of cellular contagion before germ theory gained orthodoxy.

name: Prof. Arthur Thorne
bio: Author of 'The Alembic and the Crown'. Researches Renaissance metallurgical manuscripts, furnace design, and clandestine laboratory networks.

name: Dr. Samira Chen
bio: Traces colonial botanical expeditions, botanical illustration errors that persisted for centuries, and forgotten island field notebooks.

name: Marcus Aurelius Sterling
bio: Focuses on state censorship of scientific correspondence, cipher manuscripts, telegraph diplomacy, and atomic secrecy in the 20th century.

name: Clara Lindqvist
bio: Deciphers glass plate photographic records, forgotten observatory night logs, and the early women computers whose calculations uncovered stellar composition.

name: Gabriel O'Connor
bio: Restores and analyzes brass chronometers, vacuum pumps, galvanometers, and the craft guilds whose precision made theoretical breakthroughs possible.

name: Dr. Beatrice Ramos
bio: Studies how folk remedies, sailors' navigational folklore, and indigenous metallurgy influenced formal European royal academies.

name: Thomas Finch
bio: Writes long-form narrative inquiries on scientific hubris, monumental experimental blunders, and the psychology of solitary discovery.
